To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the urban and suburban soils in Hong Kong are highly contaminated with metals, especially in the north and west parts of Hong Kong; and (2) vehicular emissions are the major source of Pb contamination in the urban soils.

(1) the surface soils of Hong Kong Island are highly enriched with metals; (2) the metal contamination is closely related to high human activity, such as traffic; and (3) the Pb isotopic ratios in the soils are closely associated with vehicular emission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial distribution of metals in the urban, suburb, and country park sites of Hong Kong.
the assessment of soil metal contamination in the urban, country park, and suburban areas in a highly urbanised city.
the distribution and sources of metal pollution in urban, suburban and country park soils, and the results will help to develop effective soil remediation strategies in Hong Kong.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the soils in urban and some suburban areas in Hong Kong Island are heavily contaminated with metals, and the major sources of metal pollution are from vehicular emissions, industrial and commercial activities, and waste incineration.
the surface soil in urban and suburban sites in Hong Kong is enriched in metals and is a potential risk to human health.
the surface soils are highly enriched with trace metals in the urban and suburban areas, whereas the country park soils are less polluted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the urban soils in Hong Kong are heavily contaminated by metals, especially Cu, Pb, Cd, and Zn, and the major source for Pb is vehicular emissions.
the metal contamination in Hong Kong soils was mainly caused by vehicular emissions, and the metal pollution was more serious in the urban areas than the suburban areas.
the metal contamination in the Hong Kong Island surface soils is related to anthropogenic inputs and the traffic conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the urban and suburban soils are contaminated with trace metals.
urbanisation and industrial development are the main sources of soil contamination.

the use of GIS and multivariate techniques can be used to produce a pollution map of trace metals, to identify the sources of metal contamination, and to assess the potential risks of soil pollution in the Hong Kong Island area.
